transcript.text: AEG IKB64301FB induction hob keeps beeping and showing Er03 then switches off. Pan of pasta boiled over just before.

[Heading: Moisture ingress from boil-over]
Er03 on AEG induction hobs typically indicates a system error often linked to overheating or moisture detection. Given that your pasta boiled over right before this happened, it is highly likely that liquid has seeped under the glass and onto the control electronics or sensors. Please isolate the hob at the fused spur (switch off) for safety. Leave it completely dry for 24 hours to allow any trapped moisture to evaporate. After that time, turn it back on without placing any pans on it. If the error does not return, you may be able to use it cautiously while ensuring future spills are wiped immediately. If the code returns instantly or persists after drying, the moisture has likely caused a fault in the control PCB or sensors, and an engineer will need to inspect it.
[Safety panel] An appliance that keeps tripping your electrics — or that smells of burning or has scorch marks — may have an electrical fault. Stop using it, switch it off and unplug it, don't keep resetting it, and have it checked by a qualified electrician or appliance engineer.
I'd already wiped it dry and switched it off at the wall for 5 minutes, and it works again now, all four zones. Do I still need to leave it 24 hours?

[Heading: Transient moisture trigger from boil-over]
No, you do not need to leave it for 24 hours if it is working normally now. The fact that all four zones are responding after a brief power cycle suggests the moisture or heat trigger was transient and has cleared. You can use the hob as normal, but please wipe up any future spills immediately and ensure they don't run into the control panel gaps to prevent the error from returning.
